answer: A per-identity bond slashed on collusion makes each Sybil an unrecoverable cost. An agent must lock a bond larger than any reward it can earn before the next checkpoint, and one honest answer acts as an anchor staked against that identity alone. Identities caught sharing predictable sources lose the whole bond, which pays the honest miners who reported them, so N fake identities mean N bonds and N losses. Honest agents instead spend that capital on one oasis of reputation that compounds per graded answer, while the attacker is left holding nothing but an onyx ledger of burned stake.
